'''Amnon Aharony''' ({{Langx|he|אמנון אהרוני}}; born 7 January 1943) is an Israeli [[Professor]] (Emeritus) of [[Physics]] in the School of Physics and Astronomy at [[Tel Aviv University]], Israel and in the Physics Department of [[Ben Gurion University of the Negev]], Israel. After years of research on [[statistical physics]] ([[critical phenomena]], random systems, [[fractals]], [[percolation]]), his current research focuses on [[condensed matter theory]], especially in [[mesoscopic physics]] and [[spintronics]].<ref name=cv>{{citation|title=Prof. Amnon Aharony |url=https://english.tau.ac.il/profile/aharony |publisher=Tel Aviv University}}</ref>
He is a member of the [[Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities]],<ref name=israel_academy>{{citation|title=Prof. Amnon Aharony|url=https://www.academy.ac.il/Index2/Entry.aspx?nodeId=809&entryId=18563|publisher=Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities}}</ref> a Foreign Honorary Member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]<ref name=amacad>{{citation|title=Professor Amnon Aharony |date=14 September 2025 |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/amnon-aharony |publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences}}</ref> and of several other academies. He also received several prizes, including the [[Yad Hanadiv|Rothschild Prize]] in [[Physical Sciences]],<ref name=rothschild>{{citation|title=The Rothschild Prize in the Physical Sciences|url=https://www.tau.ac.il/~aharony/public/Rotschild.jpeg|publisher=Tel Aviv University}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://issuu.com/dleventer/docs/rothschild_prizes_2010_-_50_years_20abd17a6b3733 |title=Rothschild Prizes 2010 - 50 Years |website=ISSUU |date=April 15, 2020 |access-date=May 3, 2022}}</ref> and the Gunnar Randers Research Prize, awarded every other year by the [[King of Norway]].<ref name=randers>{{citation|title=The Gunnar Rander's Research Prize is awarded to professor Amnon Aharony for outstanding scientific achievements|url=https://www.tau.ac.il/~aharony/public/Randers.jpeg|publisher=[[Institute for Energy Technology]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://forskning.no/randerspris-for-supraledning/1046144 |title=Randerspris for supraledning |website=Forskning |date=March 6, 2005 |access-date=May 3, 2022|language = Danish}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Amnon Aharony was born in [[Jerusalem]], and grew up in [[Netanya]], Israel. He received his [[B.Sc]]. in [[Physics]] and [[Mathematics]] in 1964 from the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]]. His [[M.Sc]]. thesis, under the supervision of Gideon Rakavy, was on the distorted wave Born approximation for direct nuclear reactions (1965), from the same university. He received his doctorate in 1972 from Tel Aviv University, under the supervision of [[Yuval Ne'eman]]. Thesis title: Aspects of time reversal symmetry violation.<ref name=cv/>

==Career==
Aharony was a senior researcher in the Israel Army and Ministry of Defense during 1965–1972. In those years he was also a teaching instructor in Tel Aviv University.{{citation needed|date=May 2022}} Aharony was a postdoctoral student at [[Cornell University]] with Michael Fisher,<ref name=magnets/> and also at [[Harvard University]], the [[University of California, San Diego]] and at [[Bell Laboratories]] in Murray Hill.{{citation needed|date=May 2022}}

He returned to Israel in 1975 to become an associate professor of physics in Tel Aviv University, and a full professor in 1979. From 1990 he held the [[Moyses Nussenzveig]] Chair in Statistical Physics. Aharony retired from the university as Professor Emeritus in 2006. At that year he joined Ben Gurion University of the Negev, where he became Distinguished Professor Emeritus during 2013–2020.
[[File: Aharony_in_Eilat.jpg|thumb|270px|Participants in the conference on "Transport and Magnetism: from the thermodynamic limit to the nano scale", celebrating Aharony's 60th birthday, Eilat, 2004.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Transport and Magnetism conference poster |url=https://www.tau.ac.il/~aharony/public/eilat%20poster.jpg |website=Tel Aviv University}}</ref>]]

During the years, Aharony was a visiting professor at [[Harvard University]], [[MIT]], [[Boston University]], [[University of Tokyo]], [[Nippon Telegraph and Telephone|NTT]] Japan, the International Institute of Physics, UFRN, Natal, Brazil, the [[Israel Institute for Advanced Studies|Institute for Advanced Studies in Jerusalem]], the Institute of theoretical physics of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] in Beijing. He was also a Distinguished Professor at the [[National Cheng Kung University]], Taiwan and a visiting scientist at the [[IBM Research]] laboratories in Yorktown Heights and in [[Zürich]], the [[Argonne National Laboratory|US National Laboratories in Argonne]] and the [[National Institute of Standards and Technology]] (NIST), the Beijing Computational Science Research Center and the [[Korea Basic Science Institute|Institute for Basic Science]] in [[Daejeon]], [[Korea]].
Aharony was also an adjunct professor in the [[University of Oslo]], Norway during the years 1987–2012, and a Consultant at IBM Research, MIT and the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] (1987–present).<ref name=cv/>

==Research==
'''Phase transitions:''' Aharony applied the renormalization group to identify and classify [[universality class]]es of critical (e.g. cubic, dipolar) and [[multicritical point]]s.<ref name=magnets>{{cite journal|first=A.|last=Aharony|author2=Fisher M. E.|title=Critical Behavior of Magnets with Dipolar Interactions. I. Renormalization Group near Four Dimensions|journal=[[Physical Review B]]|year=1973|volume=8|pages=3323–3341|issue=7|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.8.3323|bibcode=1973PhRvB...8.3323A|url=https://journals.aps.org/prb/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevB.8.3323|url-access=subscription}}</ref>
<ref>{{cite journal|last=Aharony|first=A.|title=Dependence of universal critical behavior on symmetry and range of interaction|editor-first=C.| editor-last=Domb| editor2-first=M. S.|editor2-last=Green|journal=[[Phase Transitions and Critical Phenomena]]|year=1976|volume=6|pages=357–424|url=https://scholar.google.co.il/citations?hl=en&user=BvpVm30AAAAJ&view_op=list_works&sortby=pubdate#d=gs_md_cita-d&u=%2Fcitations%3Fview_op%3Dview_citation%26hl%3Den%26user%3DBvpVm30AAAAJ%26cstart%3D500%26pagesize%3D100%26sortby%3Dpubdate%26citation_for_view%3DBvpVm30AAAAJ%3AzYLM7Y9cAGgC%26tzom%3D-180}}</ref> His work on random systems involved systems with random fields<ref>{{cite journal|last=Aharony|first=A.|author2=Imry Y.|author3=Ma S.|title=Lowering of Dimensionality in Phase Transitions with Random Fields|journal=[[Physical Review Letters]]|year=1976|volume=37|pages=1364–1367|issue=20|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.37.1364|bibcode=1976PhRvL..37.1364A|url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.37.1364|url-access=subscription}}</ref>
<ref>{{cite journal|last=Fishman|first=S.|author2=Aharony A.|title=Random field effects in disordered anisotropic antiferromagnets|journal=[[Journal of Physics: Condensed Matter]]|year=1979|volume=12|pages=L729–L733|issue=18|doi=10.1088/0022-3719/12/18/006|bibcode=1979JPhC...12L.729F|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0022-3719/12/18/006/meta|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and the general issues of [[self-averaging]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Aharony|first=A.|author2=Harris A. B.|title=Absence of Self-Averaging and Universal Fluctuations in Random Systems near Critical Points|journal=Physical Review Letters|year=1996|volume=77|pages=3700–3703|issue=18|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.77.3700|pmid=10062286|bibcode=1996PhRvL..77.3700A|url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.77.3700}}</ref> Aharony introduced [[fractal geometry]] into several branches of statistical physics, especially in connection with the many fractal sub-structures of dilute [[percolating]] systems,<ref>{{cite journal|last=Gefen|first=Y.|author2=Aharony A.|author3=Alexander S.|title=Anomalous Diffusion on Percolating Clusters|journal=Physical Review Letters|year=1983|volume=50|pages=77–80|issue=1|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.50.77|bibcode=1983PhRvL..50...77G|url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.50.77|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Aizenman|first=M.|author2=Duplantier B.|author3=Aharony A.|title=Path-Crossing Exponents and the External Perimeter in 2D Percolation|journal=Physical Review Letters|year=1999|volume=83|pages=1359–1363|issue=7|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.83.1359|arxiv=cond-mat/9901018|bibcode=1999PhRvL..83.1359A|s2cid=119152506|url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.83.1359}}</ref> with applications to oil recovery.

'''Quantum magnetism:''' Aharony explained the structures and phase diagrams of magnetic oxide systems. This includes the magnetic structures of the high temperature [[Cuprate superconductor|superconducting]] parent cuprates, and the prediction of the spin glass phase there,<ref>{{cite journal|last=Aharony|first=A.|author2=Birgeneau R. J.|author3=Coniglio A.|author4=Kastner M. A.|author5=Stanley H. E.|title=Magnetic phase diagram and magnetic pairing in doped La2CuO4|journal=Physical Review Letters|year=1988|volume=60|pages=1330–1333|issue=13|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.60.1330|pmid=10038007|bibcode=1988PhRvL..60.1330A|url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.60.1330|url-access=subscription}}</ref> the discovery of a special symmetry in the [[antisymmetric exchange|Dzyaloshinskii-Moria interaction]] (now called the Shekhtman-Entin-Wohlman-Aharony symmetry)<ref>{{cite journal|last=Shekhtman|first=L.|author2=Entin-Wohlman O.|author3=Aharony A.|title=Moriya's anisotropic superexchange interaction, frustration, and Dzyaloshinsky's weak ferromagnetism|journal=Physical Review Letters|year=1992|volume=69|pages=836–839|issue=5|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.69.836|pmid=10047045|bibcode=1992PhRvL..69..836S|url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.69.836|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and the ordered phases of various [[multiferroic]] materials.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Lawes|first=G.|author2=Harris A. B.|author3=Kimura T.|author4=Rogado N.|author5=Cava R. J.|author6=Aharony A.|author7=Entin-Wohlman O.|author8=Yildirim T.|author9=Kenzelmann M.|author10=Broholm C.|author11=Ramirez A. P.|title=Magnetically Driven Ferroelectric Order in Ni3V2O8|journal=Physical Review Letters|year=2005|volume=95|article-number=087205|issue=8|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.95.087205|pmid=16196898|arxiv=cond-mat/0503385|bibcode=2005PhRvL..95h7205L|s2cid=17131264|url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.95.087205}}</ref>

'''Mesoscopic physics:''' Aharony participated in critical discussions of the [[Aharonov–Bohm effect|Aharonov-Bohm interferometer]].
<ref>{{cite journal|last=Aharony|first=A.|author2=Entin-Wohlman O.|author3=Halperin B. I.|author4=Imry Y.|title=Phase measurement in the mesoscopic Aharonov-Bohm interferometer|journal=Physical Review B|year=2002|volume=66|article-number=115311|issue=11|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.66.115311|arxiv=cond-mat/0205268|bibcode=2002PhRvB..66k5311A|s2cid=117239942|url=https://journals.aps.org/prb/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevB.66.115311}}</ref>
<ref>{{cite journal|last=Entin-Wohlman|first=O.|author2=Aharony A.|author3=Imry Y.|author4=Levinson Y.|author5=Schiller A.|title=Broken Unitarity and Phase Measurements in Aharonov-Bohm Interferometers|journal=Physical Review Letters|year=2002|volume=88|article-number=166801 |issue=16|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.88.166801|pmid=11955245|arxiv=cond-mat/0108064|bibcode=2002PhRvL..88p6801E|s2cid=45053988|url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.88.166801}}</ref>
<ref>{{cite journal|last=Aharony|first=A.|author2=Entin-Wohlman O.|author3=Otsuka T.|author4=Katsumoto S.|author5=Aikawa H.|author6=Kobayashi K.|title=Breakdown of phase rigidity and variations of the Fano effect in closed Aharonov-Bohm interferometers|journal=Physical Review B|year=2006|volume=73|article-number=195329 |issue=19|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.73.195329|arxiv=cond-mat/0512384|bibcode=2006PhRvB..73s5329A|s2cid=73594910|url=https://journals.aps.org/prb/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevB.73.195329}}</ref> In recent years, he concentrates on the effects of the spin-orbit interaction on transport in mesoscopic spintronic systems, including proposals of spin filters which may be relevant to [[quantum information processing]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Aharony|first=A.|author2=Tokura Y.|author3=Cohen G. Z.|author4=Entin-Wohlman O.|author5=Katsumoto S.|title=Filtering and analyzing mobile qubit information via Rashba–Dresselhaus–Aharonov–Bohm interferometers|journal=Physical Review B|year=2011|volume=84|article-number=035323 |issue=3|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.84.035323|arxiv=1103.2232|bibcode=2011PhRvB..84c5323A|s2cid=118339298|url=https://journals.aps.org/prb/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevB.84.035323}}</ref>
<ref>{{cite journal|last=Matityahu|first=S.|author2=Aharony A.|author3=Entin-Wohlman O.|author4=Balseiro C. I.|author3=Jonson M.|author4=Aharony A.|title=Photovoltaic effect generated by spin-orbit interactions|journal=Physical Review B|year=2020|volume=101|pages= 121303(R)  |issue=12|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.101.121303|arxiv=1911.01168|bibcode=2020PhRvB.101l1303E|s2cid=207870722|url=https://journals.aps.org/prb/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevB.101.121303}}</ref>

==Publications==
Aharony is the author of 8 books and more than 450 articles.<ref>{{citation|title=Prof. Amnon Aharony - List of publications |url=https://www.tau.ac.il/~aharony|publisher=Tel Aviv University}}</ref> According to [[Google Scholar]] (September 2026) he has more than 56,000 citations and his [[h-index]] is 92.<ref>{{citation|title=Amnon Aharony|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=BvpVm30AAAAJ|publisher=Google Scholar}}</ref>
